outcome: Loose equality compares a Map or a Set by its contents rather than by identity

acceptance_criteria.text: Two Sets are loosely equal when every member of one loosely matches a distinct member of the other, whatever the insertion order; Sets of different size are not equal.

expected_verification.assertion: looseEqual(new Set([{a:1},{b:2}]), new Set([{b:2},{a:1}])) is true and a Set of different size is false

acceptance_criteria.text: Two Maps are loosely equal when their entries loosely match pairwise, and a Map is never loosely equal to a Set.

expected_verification.assertion: looseEqual over two Maps with matching entries is true, and looseEqual(new Map(), new Set()) is false

data_impact: None. Loose equality is a pure comparison over values already in memory; nothing is read from or written to storage.
security_impact: None directly. The comparison is quadratic in collection size and is reachable from v-model on a component, so an attacker-supplied collection of n members costs O(n squared) comparisons — bounded in practice by what a template binds, and unchanged in kind from the array comparison beside it.
rollout: Ships with the package; no flag and no staged rollout. Loose equality has no persisted state to migrate.
rollback: git revert. Before the change `looseEqual` fell through to an object comparison over own enumerable keys, which for two Maps is no keys at all — so two different Maps compared equal. A revert restores that.
